messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: raj (oncall) — High error rate and GPU OOMs reported in us-west-2 serving pool. Severity: SEV2. Dashboard: https://redwood.metrics/serving/us-west-2

raj (oncall): On it. Quick summary? which model, any customer impact yet?

sarah (eng-runtime): Seeing repeated CUDA OOMs in logs for model: open-llm-xl-v2 on cluster serving-usw2-gpu-3. Autoscaler is spiking replicas from 8 -> 32 -> 6 repeatedly (thrash). Pods starting then immediately CrashLoopBackOff with OOM on init.

linda (eng-sre): Can you paste a representative log tail?

sarah (eng-runtime): Sure — here's a recent container log from one of the crashing pods:

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 12.5 GiB (GPU 0), free 2.1 GiB
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] ERROR runtime: Aborting request, freeing KV cache
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] container_kill: OOM Killed
[2026-03-15T09:12:07Z] pod: crashloopbackoff
```

mike (infra): Autoscaler logs show rapid scale decisions because of CPU+GPU utilization spikes on the service LB. Looks like a traffic surge hitting long-context requests which blow up memory. The HPA target is a combination metric; it's incorrectly reacting to transient spikes.

raj (oncall): Customer impact? Elaine?

elaine (support): Support reports 15 accounts seeing increased latency; 4 customers reporting 502s. No enterprise SLA hits yet but page came from internal monitoring. Customers on Dedicated pools in us-west-2 may be affected. I'm drafting a status notice.

sarah (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: Autoscaler is over-reacting to a small number of heavy requests, creating many new pods that rehydrate big KV caches and push nodes into OOM. Also suspect a recent runtime image (rtd-1.44) introduced a change in GPU memory pre-allocation.

linda (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation plan (short window):
- Pause autoscaler scale-ups, set maxReplicas to current 8
- Increase scale-down cooldown to 10m to avoid flip-flopping
- Pin model to smaller variant open-llm-xl-v2-quant for new pods
- If nodes show Kernel OOMs, cordon + drain affected nodes and reprovision

raj (oncall): I'll apply a temporary maxReplicas cap and disable aggressive scale-ups. Can someone run the commands?

mike (infra): Running kubectl patch now.

```
kubectl -n serving patch hpa serving-open-llm-xl --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":8}}'
kubectl -n serving patch hpa serving-open-llm-xl --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}}'
```

mike (infra): Patch applied. Autoscaler no longer exceeding 8. Note: existing crashloop pods remain — need to restart them with the pinned image or model config.

sarah (eng-runtime): I'll roll a controlled restart to force new pods to use the quantized variant and reduced KV cache size. Doing a canary of 2 pods first.

deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for serving-open-llm-xl -> image: runtime-rtd-1.44-quant (2 pods)

sarah (eng-runtime): Canary deployed. Monitoring logs and memory.

(2 minutes pass)

sarah (eng-runtime): Canary pods healthy, memory stable ~6.1 GiB usage. No OOMs so far. Latency ~+40ms.

linda (eng-sre): Good. Roll the rest but keep maxReplicas=8 and disable further scale-ups for 30m. Also schedule a cordon/drain for node-03-usw2-gpu which reported repeated kernel OOMs.

mike (infra): Cordon + drain started for node-03-usw2-gpu:
```
kubectl cordon node-03-usw2-gpu
kubectl drain node-03-usw2-gpu --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

raj (oncall): Elaine — can we send a short customer-facing update: what happened, that we're mitigating with autoscaler cap and rolling to smaller variant, ETA 30–45m?

elaine (support): Drafting now. Will mention limited impact to some customers, mitigation in progress, next update in 30m.

sarah (eng-runtime): After rolling remaining pods to quant variant and draining the bad node, OOMs stopped. Autoscaler remains capped. I'm seeing request success rate return to baseline.

mike (infra): Note: during the thrash we briefly exhausted GPU slice allocations on the node pool causing node flaps — cloud provider reported transient driver restarts. We're provisioning 2 spare nodes to prevent immediate pressure.

raj (oncall): Handoff: I'm going to sleep-cycle off in 20m. Linda, can you take primary oncall for follow-ups and postmortem? I'll remain reachable by ping.

linda (eng-sre): Taking over. I'll keep the cap in place and open a follow-up incident with logs and an action item: tune autoscaler metric to ignore single-pod heavy requests, and revert to prior runtime image if needed.

sarah (eng-runtime): Action items for postmortem:
- Reproduce memory regression in rtd-1.44 vs rtd-1.43
- Add autoscaler smoothing (percentile-based metric) and longer stabilization
- Add pre-warming mitigations for KV cache (lazy rehydrate)
- Improve alert to differentiate sustained high QPS vs bursty long-context requests

elaine (support): I'll send customers the 30m update. Assigning Severity: SEV2 -> monitoring for SLA risk.

mike (infra): Infra note: disable auto-scale-up triggers from GPU memory metric until autoscaler tuned.

raj (oncall): Thanks team. Closing active paging loop. Leaving the thread for postmortem notes. If anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:
